question: One-third of a work is finished in four days by P and one-fourth of the same work is finished in six days by Q. P and Q together work for six days and the rest of the work is finished by R in two days. R alone can finish the whole work in _____ days.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time taken by P to finish the whole work = 4 × 3 = 12 days, and Q = 6 × 4 = 24 days.

Let Total Work = LCM(12, 24) = 24 units.

Efficiency of P = 2 units/day, Q = 1 unit/day ⇒ P + Q = 3 units/day.

Work done by P and Q in 6 days = 6 × 3 = 18 units.

Remaining work = 24 − 18 = 6 units, which is done by R in 2 days ⇒ R's efficiency = 3 units/day.

Time taken by R alone to complete the work = 24 ÷ 3 = 8 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P to complete 1/3 of the work = 4 days

Time taken by Q to complete 1/4 of the work = 6 days

Time worked by P and Q together = 6 days

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total time taken by P to complete the whole work = 4 × 3 = 12 days

⇒ Total time taken by Q to complete the whole work = 6 × 4 = 24 days

⇒ R finishes the remaining 6 units in 2 days, so the Efficiency of R = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 units/day

⇒ Time taken by R alone to finish the whole work (24 units) = 24 ÷ 3 = 8 days

**∴ The correct answer is 8 days.**

Pipes & Cisterns

Functions exactly like Time and Work, but an outlet pipe has a negative efficiency. If an inlet fills the tank in X hours and an outlet empties it in Y hours, the net filling capacity in 1 hour is (1/X − 1/Y).

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in direct proportion to the actual amount of work done by each person. If all persons work for the same number of days, the total wages are divided directly in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Days Work

If two people A and B work on alternate days, find the combined work done in a single 2-day cycle. Then multiply this cycle to approach the total work closely before calculating the time needed to finish the remainder.
